before: Square brackets can select elements using an HTML attribute. [data-tags="urgent"] requires the whole value to equal urgent. [data-tags~="urgent"] instead looks for urgent as one word in a space-separated list.

The custom data-tags attribute stores text for this example; it does not itself change styling. ~= matches a complete list token, so urgently is not urgent. ^= tests whether the value begins with the supplied text; it does not require a whole token. Quoted values belong inside the square brackets.

```html

One

Two

Three

``` ```css p { color: navy; } [data-tags~="urgent"] { color: teal; } ```

Make only elements containing the complete urgent token teal; leave urgently navy. The supplied HTML stays in index.html; edit the CSS. The checks inspect this small page, not every possible browser or accessibility requirement.
after: An attribute is a setting in an HTML starting tag. A CSS selector in square brackets can check an attribute. `[data-tags="urgent"]` needs the entire `data-tags` value to be `urgent`.

The `~=` sign checks for one whole word in a list separated by spaces. `[data-tags~="urgent"]` matches both `urgent` and `draft urgent`. It does not match `urgently`. The `^=` sign has a different job: it checks the start of the text, even if that text is only part of a word.
The order of the words does not matter to `~=`. Both `draft urgent` and `urgent draft` contain the whole word `urgent`. Check that the note marked `urgently` stays navy.

before.question: An attribute changes from data-tags="draft urgent" to data-tags="urgent draft". Does [data-tags~="urgent"] still match?
choices: No; ~= requires the entire attribute to equal urgent.
Yes; urgent is still a complete space-separated token.
before.explanation: Token membership does not depend on whether that token comes first. A prefix selector would ask a different question.

after.question: data-tags changes from "draft urgent" to "urgent draft". Does [data-tags~="urgent"] still match?
choices: No. The word urgent must be first.
No. The whole value must be urgent.
Yes. The list still contains the whole word urgent.
after.explanation: The word is still in the list. Its position does not matter.
